variants.name: serde derive attributes at the format boundary
variants.implementation_notes: serde's attribute set is the translator: #[serde(rename = "order_id")] and #[serde(rename_all = "camelCase")] handle key differences, #[serde(deserialize_with = "path")] and serialize_with carry value-level conversions, and #[serde(default)] versus deny_unknown_fields encode the tolerance policy (serde.rs field and container attributes). What replaces the classic structure is the derived Serialize/Deserialize impl selected by the format crate (serde_json, rmp-serde, or prost for Protobuf); a hand-written translator is still the better tool for in-process translation between two canonical models, where serde plays no part.
pitfalls: deny_unknown_fields makes any producer-side addition a decode error, while omitting it silently ignores typos in the wire contract - the tolerant-reader trade-off has to be a conscious choice per contract.
deserialize_with is not called for an Option field whose key is absent (missing and null are different); combine it with default when a field may be omitted, or the custom conversion never runs.
#[serde(untagged)] and flattened maps hide the mapping, and their errors carry no field path, so a malformed message arrives as "data did not match any variant" with nothing to diagnose.

variants.name: std conversion traits (From/TryFrom) for in-process mapping
variants.idiom_name: impl From<Legacy> for Canonical / TryFrom with a typed error
variants.implementation_notes: When both shapes are Rust types you already own, the translation is an inherent or standard conversion rather than a serialisation concern: impl From<LegacyOrder> for Order for total mappings and impl TryFrom<LegacyOrder> for Order with a typed error for the fallible ones (use std::convert). This keeps the translation in the type system, makes .into() the call site, and leaves serde free to describe only the wire layer; choose it when the seam is internal and no foreign format is involved.
pitfalls: TryFrom plus an untyped Box<dyn Error> loses the invalid-message classification the routing needs; use a dedicated error enum per seam.
From impls are total by definition, so a lossy mapping implemented as From silently discards fields instead of surfacing them as TryFrom errors.
